title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a smooth family of curves f: X -> S (analytic, or differentiable in s), relative 1-forms ω_s on the fibres X_s, and a derivation D on S lifted locally to a vector field (derivation) D̄ on X; this local lift is what the page calls a 'connection'. Sections a(s), b(s) of X -> S are 'horizontal' when they are integral curves of the lift, so that for any function g, D_s(g(a(s))) = (D̄g)(a(s)). The goal is the differentiation-under-the-integral formula of the previous page, (3): D_s ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} ω_s = ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} (D̄ω)_s. This is the transcendental characterisation of the Gauss–Manin connection on periods. It is then used to show that a Picard–Fuchs-type condition (7) (presumably: Σ D̄_i ω_i is relatively exact) implies that the operator Σ D_i ⊗ ω_i kills all periods.

Local step (top of page). Near s0, with a(s0) and b(s0) close, write ω = dφ relatively. The left side of (3) is then D_s(φ(b(s)) − φ(a(s))) = (D̄φ)(b(s)) − (D̄φ)(a(s)), using horizontality. The right side is ∫ D̄dφ = ∫ d(D̄φ), because the Lie derivative commutes with d. This also equals (D̄φ)(b) − (D̄φ)(a). So the two sides agree, and the general case follows by subdividing the path and transporting the subdivision points horizontally.

Formula (14). Conversely, for horizontal a, b, the pairing μ(a,b) = ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} (Σ D̄_i ω_i)_s equals φ(b(s)) − φ(a(s)), where φ is the relative primitive given by (10).

Announced step (sufficiency of (7) for the validity of (3)). It is to be shown that Σ_i D_{is} ∫_{C_s} ω_{is} = 0 for every 1-chain C_s varying differentiably with s whose boundary is horizontal. Equivalently, Σ_i D_{is} ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} ω_{is} = 0 for horizontal sections a, b near s. The proof continues on the next page by working locally in a small open set of X where a lift exists.

In modern terms this is the elementary verification that the Gauss–Manin connection is computed by Lie derivative along a lift and differentiation under the integral sign. Integrals over paths with horizontal endpoints are handled in the style of relative cohomology, and periods are annihilated by an operator Σ D_i ω_i exactly when Σ D̄_i ω_i is relatively exact. That is the standard criterion behind Picard–Fuchs equations.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument is a sketch: horizontality of a, b is relative to the chosen local lift D̄. The independence of the result from the lift (the change of lift alters D̄ω by a relatively exact term plus a boundary contribution) is implicitly handled by the horizontal-endpoint condition but not stated.
The local existence of a relative primitive φ with ω = dφ near a short path, and the existence of a lift D̄ on a neighbourhood, are assumed without comment. Both are standard for smooth morphisms.

ideas.what: Differentiation of period integrals under the integral sign via a lift D̄ of a base vector field, using that D̄ commutes with d
ideas.modern_name: Transcendental description of the Gauss–Manin connection (Lie derivative along a lift)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Picard, Fuchs); modern form Manin 1958, Katz–Oda 1968, Deligne 1970
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1966 letter to Atiyah and 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' treat algebraic de Rham cohomology; Gauss–Manin was developed by Katz–Oda following his ideas

ideas.what: Integrals between horizontal sections a(s), b(s) as periods of relative cohomology; reduction of cycles with horizontal boundary to paths
ideas.modern_name: Periods of relative cohomology H^1(X_s, {a(s), b(s)}) and their Gauss–Manin connection

ideas.what: Criterion that Σ D_i ∫ ω_i = 0 for all horizontal-boundary cycles iff Σ D̄_i ω_i is relatively exact (condition (7))
ideas.modern_name: Picard–Fuchs equation as a relation in relative de Rham cohomology (Griffiths–Dwork reduction)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an expository verification of the standard differentiation-under-the-integral property of the Gauss–Manin connection and its link with Picard–Fuchs operators. This is well-known material, carefully but routinely worked out.
